title: Mass Spectrometry Protocol for Tear Fluid Proteome Profiling and Biomarker Discovery
author: Juul-Elbaek, Peiris-Pagès, et al.
materials: Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay, or

steps.title: Activate SPE cartridge
steps.instruction: Prepare the SOLA‑μ plate for peptide binding by sequentially conditioning it with methanol and buffers, centrifuging after each addition.

substeps.instruction: Place the SOLA‑μ plate in a 96‑well waste plate.
Add 200 µL LC/MS‑grade methanol.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at room temperature; discard the flow‑through.
Add 200 µL Buffer B.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at room temperature; discard the flow‑through.
Add 200 µL Buffer C.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at room temperature; discard the flow‑through.
Repeat the Buffer C wash (add 200 µL Buffer C, centrifuge as above).
Store Buffer C at 18 °C–24 °C for up to 3 months.

steps.title: Load digested peptides onto SPE
steps.instruction: Transfer acid‑ified peptide digests onto the activated SPE plate and centrifuge to bind peptides.

substeps.instruction: Transfer digested peptides (200–1,000 µL per well) using low‑retention tips to the 96‑well SOLA plate (process in batches as needed).
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at 18 °C–24 °C; discard the flow‑through each time.
If desired, store half of the sample at –80 °C for future analysis.

steps.title: Wash SPE with Buffer A
steps.instruction: Remove residual contaminants by washing the bound peptides with Buffer A.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL Buffer A.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at 18 °C–24 °C; discard the flow‑through.
Repeat the Buffer A wash (add 200 µL Buffer A, centrifuge as above).

steps.title: Elute peptides from SPE
steps.instruction: Recover the purified peptides by eluting them with Buffer D into a LoBind PCR plate.

substeps.instruction: Place the washed SOLA plate into a clean LoBind 96‑well PCR plate.
Add 30 µL Buffer D.
Centrifuge at 450 × g for 1 min at 18 °C–24 °C.
Add a second 30 µL of Buffer D.
Centrifuge again at 450 × g for 1 min at 18 °C–24 °C (final eluate volume = 60 µL).
Store Buffer D at 18 °C–24 °C for up to 3 months.

steps.title: Seal and store peptide eluates
steps.instruction: Prepare the eluates for long‑term storage and downstream LC‑MS analysis.

substeps.instruction: Seal the LoBind PCR plate containing the 60 µL eluates with a new adhesive cover.
Optional: measure peptide concentration using either the Pierce Quantitative Colorimetric Peptide Assay or a NanoDrop at A205.
Store the sealed plate at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine peptide concentration
steps.instruction: Quantify peptide amount prior to LC‑MS using UV absorbance.

substeps.instruction: Measure absorbance at 280 nm with a NanoPhotometer N60 (or equivalent spectrophotometer).
Calculate concentration using the instrument’s software or standard curve.

description: Proteins represent essential targets in the search for biomarkers, as they can signal healthy or diseased states, responses to pharmacological interventions, and other relevant clinical information. To date, over 15,000 different proteins have been identified in major human body fluids.1 The most commonly studied plasma proteome exhibits an exceptionally broad dynamic range, spanning up to 10–12 orders of magnitude, primarily due to the presence of highly abundant proteins such as albumin and immunoglobulins. This complexity necessitates depletion strategies to enable the detection of low-abundance biomarkers. Tear fluid proteomics is gaining attention for biomarker discovery due to its non-invasive collection, and despite their small volume (3-10 μL), rich proteome, with a protein concentration ranging from 6 to 11 mg/mL.2,3,4,5 In healthy individuals, human tears contain >1,000 proteins.5 Unlike the collection of plasma or cerebrospinal fluid, tear fluid collection is minimally invasive, making tears an ideal source for biomarker discovery for diagnostic, prognostic and monitoring purposes.4 This study presents an optimized protocol for the extraction, digestion and preparation of tear fluid proteins, with a focus on maximizing protein recovery, minimizing contaminants, and achieving higher reproducibility, all of which are critical for clinical proteomics. Our protocol details the isolation and processing of tear fluid collected using the Schirmer strip test for Liquid Chromatography-Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) analysis.6 Before starting, define research goals and control factors affecting protein stability (e.g., temperature). Prepare all reagents and equipment in advance. This 5-h protocol improves tear proteome reliability, supporting clinical proteomics, biomarker discovery, and personalized medicine.
